our_argument_summary: WIN-042 ('Global magnetic field decays at rate >=28 nT/year') is mathematically equivalent to WIN-037 ('field decayed >=28 nT in 12 months'); both are confirmed off the same single SAA-core observation (INTERMAGNET Tsumeb, ~30 nT drop), the 28 nT/yr figure is a dome model input parameter (raw-text/05-model.txt:42), and the global dipole decline (~5%/century, Thebault et al. 2015 IGRF-12) falls well below the threshold. Verdict 'Misleading' for WIN-count inflation: one observation counted twice.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: SAA-core decay (20-35 nT/yr) and global dipole decline (~5%/century) are standard geomagnetism, documented by IGRF/WMM/INTERMAGNET for decades (Thebault et al. 2015, doi:10.1186/s40623-015-0228-9 — verified via Crossref this run). The dome renames the driver 'aetheric field decay'; the numbers are unchanged.

code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The value appears only in the parameter table (05-model.txt:42,75). No formula connects disc_radius, firmament_height, or any dome parameter to 28 nT/yr. The 'projected 2030: -32 nT/year' on line 75 is trend extrapolation, not geometric derivation.

holes_found.description: NEW (quantitative): detail_evidence states the global decline is 'approximately 15 nT/yr in globally averaged surface intensity'. 15 nT/yr follows from 5%/century of the ~30,000 nT EQUATORIAL dipole field; a proper surface average of dipole intensity carries factor ~1.38 (mean |B| ~41,400 nT), giving ~20.7 nT/yr for the same 5%/century. Both values sit below the 28 nT/yr threshold, so the argument survives, but the label 'globally averaged' attached to the equatorial-basis number is technically wrong and is the single easiest line for a defender to attack.
holes_found.recommendation: Rephrase to: 'the equatorial dipole intensity declines ~15 nT/yr; averaged over the whole surface, ~21 nT/yr — either basis falls below the 28 nT/yr threshold.' Same fix applies to WIN-037, which carries the identical sentence.

holes_found.description: NEW (cross-WIN surface tension): WIN-042 says 'the >=28 nT/yr threshold is met at SAA-core stations (Tsumeb: ~30 nT/yr)' while WIN-037 argues the dome's own confirmation annualizes BELOW threshold ('~30 nT over 14 months = 25.7 nT/yr — below the dome's own 28 nT/yr threshold'). Reconcilable (long-run Tsumeb rate vs the dome's specific 14-month window) but a critic can quote the two sentences side-by-side as 'your review contradicts itself'.
holes_found.recommendation: Add one clause to WIN-042's detail_evidence: 'met at SAA-core stations on the long-run rate (~30 nT/yr at Tsumeb), though the dome's own 14-month confirmation window annualizes to only 25.7 nT/yr — see WIN-037'.

stronger_arguments.description: The dome's own live dashboard now monitors field decay at 77.0 nT/yr (PRED=OBS identity at TTB) while WIN-037/042 celebrate >=28 nT/yr. Three different 'predictions' of the same observable now coexist (28 cumulative, 28 rate, 77 live panel) — each at whatever value the relevant dataset happened to show. This is threshold-shopping across surfaces and is a stronger framing of the duplication critique than rate-vs-cumulative equivalence alone.

kernel_of_truth.description: The underlying observation is real and well-measured: the SAA-core field at Tsumeb declines at roughly 30 nT/yr on the long-run INTERMAGNET record (raw-text/08-live-power.txt:230 cites 'INTERMAGNET TTB annual means'), and the dome's parameter table honestly dates its 28 nT/yr figure to '2000-2025' observation (raw-text/05-model.txt:75). The dome is tracking a genuine, scientifically interesting geomagnetic feature.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Tracking a 25-year-old published trend is not predicting it: the dome's own '(2000-2025)' annotation (raw-text/05-model.txt:75) concedes the value was known at write-time, and the legitimate-novelty carve-out in our post-hoc standard (detail_verdict_text, #posthoc-standard anchor — verified present in sections.json this run) requires data 'not plausibly known to the author at write-time'. And whatever credit the observation earns, it can be earned once — WIN-037 already claims it; WIN-042 adds a second label to the same measurement (data/wins.json:042 finding: 'Mathematically equivalent to WIN-037').

advocate_mode.best_defense: 'WIN-037 was a closed 12-month window test; WIN-042 is a STANDING rate claim that exposes the model to falsification every future year. A window claim and a persistent-rate claim are operationally different predictions — the second keeps risking refutation after the first is banked. Also, your own page admits the threshold IS met at SAA-core stations, and your global counter-figure of 15 nT/yr is computed on the equatorial field; the honest surface-average is over 20 nT/yr, uncomfortably close to 28 given measurement spread.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Two fixes neutralize this: (1) note that a standing rate claim only adds falsification exposure if something monitors it — and the dome monitors 77.0 nT/yr at TTB, not 28 nT/yr globally (monitoring tag 'none'); (2) repair the 15-vs-21 nT/yr basis as per holes_found[0] so the 'your number is wrong' wedge disappears. With both, the defense drops to rating 1-2.

(2) WIN-037's 'live Domain 8 panel' label is stale against the current V51 dashboard where the numbered Domain 8 is Lunar Magnetic Tide and the SAA panel is unnumbered in the live table — cosmetic, flag for WIN-037's next cycle rather than a patch from this review. (3) Shared uncited-basis sentence ('~15 nT/yr globally averaged') appears in both WIN-037 and WIN-042 — fix both together.

quantitative_verification.computations: 5%/century of 30,000 nT (equatorial) = 15.0 nT/yr — reproduces our figure but on the equatorial basis. Surface-averaged dipole intensity factor numerically integrated: 1.38 -> mean field ~41,400 nT -> 20.7 nT/yr. 30*12/14 = 25.7 nT/yr — matches WIN-037's claim exactly. All below the 28 nT/yr threshold; core argument robust to basis choice.

deeper_analysis: Two months after c2, the dome-side picture has shifted in ways that strengthen the duplication critique without changing the verdict. The live dashboard now runs a field-decay identity check at 77.0 nT/yr (TTB annual means, 20% tolerance) while the WIN pair being reviewed celebrates >=28 nT/yr — meaning the dome maintains three coexisting 'predicted' values for one observable, each calibrated to whatever its source dataset shows. Meanwhile the dome's home page restructured to '39 Confirmed Wins | 24 Pending', and WIN-042's verbatim text has never been captured in raw-text — we are reviewing our inference of the dome's claim, which has been acceptable so far (the parameter table and WIN-037 equivalence carry the argument) but should be closed out before this WIN is cited in any headline material. The quantitative audit found our only soft spot: the '~15 nT/yr globally averaged' figure is equatorial-basis arithmetic wearing a global-average label; the honest surface-average (~21 nT/yr) still sits below threshold, so the fix is cosmetic but should be applied to both WINs carrying the sentence. No critical or major findings; no alert entry warranted.
